data.reason: Original author-hosted manuscript of Nees, Helbein and Porter, Speech Auditory Alerts Promote Memory for Alerted Events in a Video-Simulated Self-Driving Car Ride, was inspected via web PDF renderer on 2026-11-10. E1 appears satisfied: Methods Participants, PDF index 9/printed manuscript p. 10, reports recruited N=90 and analysed N=85 after five exclusions. E2/G01: original manuscript pp. 11–12 specifies machine-issued car-status/hazard alerts; speech via TTS engine versus naturalistic auditory icons (water, air hiss, horns, etc.), not merely ambient vehicle audio. E3: one between-subject study with three conditions, visual text control, auditory icons and speech; randomly assigned participants. E4: memory recall of alerted events, effort/workload, annoyance and confidence/usability ratings, with Results visible pp. 14–16. E5: original Methods and Results available, primary experiment, no review-only design. E6: original first-published online 2016-02-16 and printed May 2016; before cutoff 2026-10-04. Thus E1–E6 are provisionally supported for this AUTHOR MANUSCRIPT edition, not an authenticated SAGE version of record. There is ONE described experiment across three arms; multiple videos, tasks, analyses and arms are not independent studies or independent samples. No originality claim relative to other Nees papers, sample-independence determination or numeric extraction. Under protocol §10 tool-mediated reading can support eligibility screening, but current record_graph v1 requires performed manifestation-bound AID for full_text include/exclude and this source has no canonical manifestation or reading event. Therefore pending preserves the exact engineering/provenance gate rather than falsely asserting final admission.
